## Task 32: `GET /home` — the wire shapes, and the first client-facing route since M5

M6 declined routes and delivered through the CLI, and three milestones before
it did the same, so the default here is CLI-only. **Boundary call 1 in full,
and its full argument goes in the route's own docstring rather than only in
this plan** — a boundary call recorded only in a plan document is one the next
reader of `routers/home.py` cannot find:

> **1. `GET /home` IS built, and this is the first milestone since M5 to add a
> client-facing route.** M6 declined a route and delivered through the CLI,
> and three milestones before it did the same, so the default here is
> CLI-only. Four things override it:
>
> - **ADR-0006 is the ADR that governs this milestone and its entire content
>   is about the route.** *"The server composes. `/home` returns ordered,
>   hydrated rows; clients render them in order."* Its central claim — *"One
>   request paints a screen, which is what makes the home screen feel instant
>   over a slow link"* — is a property of a request boundary and is not
>   observable through a CLI at all. M6's boundary call 1 declined a route for
>   capabilities the CLI genuinely delivers (`search`, `suggest`, `similar`
>   each print exactly what the route would return). Composition is the first
>   capability where the CLI is a *proxy* for the deliverable rather than the
>   deliverable in another skin.
> - **`row.invalidated` is assigned to M7 by name** (PRD 07's SSE table, and
>   `ports/events.py`'s own docstring says the member is absent *"because
>   nothing composes a row until M7"*). An invalidation event with no row to
>   invalidate is an event with no consumer, which is the thing this project
>   refuses.
> - **M5's precedent covers the missing error envelope.** PRD 07's RFC 9457
>   vocabulary is M9's, and M5 built `GET /titles/{id}` without it for a
>   stated reason: *"M5 has no request whose honest answer is a domain-level
>   failure."* `GET /home` has exactly that property — PRD 08's degradation
>   table says *"LLM call fails → Home composes without them"*, and every
>   other input is local state. There is no 503 here to give a `code` to.
> - **`usher home` ships too**, because PRD 08's operator rule is that *"every
>   one of them has to work against an empty database"*, and a route is a poor
>   place to find out that composition divides by zero on a household that has
>   watched nothing.
>
> **What is still M9's, so this call is a route and not a land grab:** the RFC
> 9457 envelope, `usher.http.server.duration`,
> `usher.cache.hits`/`.misses`, HTTP cache headers, and pagination. `GET
> /home` returns the whole screen in one response with no cursor, which is
> what ADR-0006 specifies and what PRD 07's own endpoint table shows
> (`/browse` carries a cursor; `/home` does not).

**No cursor**, and it is settled twice over: ADR-0006 says the server composes
a *screen*, and PRD 07's own endpoint table gives `/browse` a
`&cursor=` and gives `/home` none. A cursor on `/home` would be a client
paging through *rows*, which is a browse under a screen's name.

**`display_hint` is `portrait | landscape | wide | square`**, and it is
ADR-0006's only concrete vocabulary: *"Rows carry a display *hint* (`portrait |
landscape | wide | square`) but never a layout."* A hint is what a card is
shaped like; a layout is how many fit, how they scroll, and what the client
does at 320 px. The DTO carries the first and nothing that implies the second
— no `columns`, no `card_width`, no `rows_visible`.

**The wire enum question, settled against the repo's own two precedents.**
`api/dto/events.py` mints its own `SseEventKind` and maps to it, because there
is **no `response_model`** on a `StreamingResponse` and the shape is therefore
asserted in a test rather than described in `/openapi.json`.
`api/dto/title.py` does the opposite: it reuses `EnrichmentState`, `HdrFormat`
and `TitleKind` from `domain/enums`. `GET /home` has a `response_model`, so it
follows `dto/title.py` — a rename of `DisplayHint` is a visible diff in
`/openapi.json` and a mypy error at the DTO, which is the deliberateness PRD
07 asks for. The reason is written down in the DTO so the divergence from
`dto/events.py` reads as a decision.

**No artwork on a card — boundary call 3, and the DTO documents its own
absence the way `dto/title.py` does:**

> **3. `RowCard` carries no artwork field, exactly as `GET /titles/{id}`
> carries no `images` key.** PRD 06 describes `RowCard` as carrying *"artwork
> refs"*, and there is no `Image` table, no `images` column, and not even a
> `poster_path` on `titles`. M9 owns the image proxy and the table. The choice
> is between an always-null field and no field, and M5 already settled the
> identical question one route over, in a sentence this call reuses verbatim:
> *"an empty list would be indistinguishable from a film with no cast."* A
> `RowCard` with `"artwork": null` on every card of every row is a
> client-side branch that never takes its other arm, and the day M9 fills it,
> every client that shipped against the null already renders without it.

**The route holds no `SourceAdapter`, and that is structural rather than a
caught exception.** PRD 08: *"a degraded subsystem narrows functionality; it
never fails a request local state can answer."* Every input to a composed
screen is local — watch state, media items, `title_neighbors`, `user_taste`,
`genome_scores`, credits. There is no call to fail, so there is no 503 and
nothing for an RFC 9457 `code` to name.

**Asserted on imports**, and the two misses the repository already measured
must both be handled:

- a signature check spelled `parameter.annotation in (SourceAdapter, ...)` (or
  via `annotation.__name__`) **does not see a string annotation**, which is
  the one form needing no import at all;
- an `ast.ImportFrom`-only scan **does not see `import usher.ports.source`**.

So: read every annotation as *text*, and walk both `ast.Import` and
`ast.ImportFrom`. Precedent: `tests/unit/test_services_titles.py`. The scan
covers `usher.services.home` **and every module in `ROW_PROVIDERS`** — nine
providers is nine chances for one of them to reach for an adapter, and a scan
of the composer alone reads as coverage while checking one ninth of the
surface. That is the same lesson M6's sweep recorded when a guard scoped to
the class docstring missed the method's.

**Against an empty database, and the answer is argued rather than assumed.**
With no watch state, no embeddings, no `title_neighbors`, no credits and no
media items, every provider proposes nothing, nothing is built, and the
response is **`200 {"rows": []}`**.

- **Not a 500.** Nothing raised; there was nothing to compute.
- **Not a 404.** `/home` is a screen, not a resource, and a screen with
  nothing on it is a fact about the household rather than a missing thing.
- **And deliberately not padded.** The tempting alternative — one "popular
  titles" row so the screen is never empty — is *precisely* the failure this
  milestone's rule 2 names: it produces a screen that looks personalised on a
  household that has watched nothing, and it is the one that survives review.
  An empty `rows` list is **distinguishable**; a generic row is not.
- **The case that separates "no signal" from "no data" is the more useful
  one.** A household with a synced library but no watch state is not empty:
  `media_items.added_at` exists, so `RecentlyAddedProvider` fires and the
  screen is one row. Both cases ship, and the pair is what makes `rows: []`
  readable as "nothing here yet" rather than as "composition is broken".

**`deps.py` wiring — what M7 adds and what stays on `app.state`.**

Request-scoped providers (the ports, never the `Postgres*` classes, per the
module's own rule): the new repositories groups B, E, F and G land
(`PersonRepository`, `CreditRepository`, `CollectionRepository`,
`GenomeRepository`, `TasteRepository`), then `RowContext`, then `HomeService`.

On `app.state`: the `RowCache` (Task 31 — one per process; a request-scoped
cache caches nothing, exactly as a request-scoped bus fans out to nobody).

**And no embedder, which is the interesting one.** `deps.py:426-435` argues
the general case already and this task reuses it rather than re-deriving it:

> `EnrichService` is deliberately absent … It needs a `MetadataProvider`,
> whose only implementation owns the token bucket that keeps this deployment
> under TMDb's ~40 rps ceiling — and a request-scoped `TmdbClient` gives every
> concurrent request a *fresh* bucket, so N in-flight requests get N × 30 rps.
> The bucket has to outlive a request, which makes it a lifespan resource on
> `app.state` rather than a `Depends`.

The embedder is one-per-process on identical terms — a 65 MB ONNX session and
a 4.84 s cold load. **So if this path needed one it would go on `app.state`,
and it does not need one**: every row reads a *precomputed* artefact.
`BecauseYouWatchedProvider` reads `title_neighbors`; `GenreAffinityProvider`
reads the stored centroid in `user_taste`. Computing those needs a model;
reading them does not — the same property `usher index` already has (*"loads
no model at all: staleness is a question about a recorded model **name**"*).

That matches the front matter's own G → I handoff (*"`HomeService` must
compose without one when the deployment has no embedder"*) and it is worth a
case, because the failure it prevents is a home screen that 500s in every
push-only deployment: `create_app`'s lifespan builds the model **only when
`worker_enabled`**, so a route that reached for one would work in development
and fail in exactly the deployment PRD 08 describes.

**`tests/integration/test_pipeline_deps.py` must grow every new provider.** It
is the only thing in this repository that resolves the dependency graph FastAPI
actually builds, and the failure it catches has no other detector: annotating
one dependency without `Depends` raises `FastAPIError` at **route
registration**, and a unit test that overrides `get_home_service` never sees
it. Its own count assertion grows too.

**Files:**
- Create: `src/usher/api/dto/home.py`, `src/usher/api/routers/home.py`
- Create: `tests/unit/test_api_home.py`
- Modify: `src/usher/api/deps.py`, `src/usher/api/app.py`,
  `tests/integration/test_pipeline_deps.py`,
  `tests/integration/test_pipeline_spans.py`, `docs/prd/07-client-api.md`

```python
# src/usher/api/dto/home.py
"""`GET /home` (ADR-0006, PRD 06, PRD 07).

**A card carries no artwork, and the absence is documented rather than
filled with a null** -- the same choice `dto/title.py` makes for `images`,
`credits`, `similar` and the season hierarchy, and for the sentence M5
wrote for it: an always-null field is a client-side branch that never takes
its other arm, and the day M9 lands the image proxy and its table, every
client that shipped against the null already renders without it. There is
no `Image` table, no `images` column and not even a `poster_path` on
`titles` (M7 boundary call 3).

**No cursor.** ADR-0006 composes a *screen*, and PRD 07's endpoint table
gives `/browse` a cursor and gives `/home` none. Paging through rows would
be a browse under a screen's name. Pagination on this surface is M9's.

**`display_hint` is a hint, never a layout** -- ADR-0006's only concrete
vocabulary, `portrait | landscape | wide | square`. A hint is what a card
is shaped like; a layout is how many fit, how they scroll, and what a
client does at 320 px. Nothing here carries a column count, a card width or
a visible-row count, and the day one is asked for, ADR-0006's own
mitigation is the answer: an optional layout *profile* that constrains
composition, not a layout in the response.

**`DisplayHint` is the domain enum, not a wire twin, and that is the
opposite of what `dto/events.py` does.** The reason is `response_model`:
this route has one, so `/openapi.json` describes the vocabulary and a
rename is a visible schema diff plus a mypy error here -- which is the
deliberateness PRD 07 asks for. `SseEventKind` exists precisely because a
`StreamingResponse` is bytes and FastAPI's serializer never sees it, so
that surface has no schema to make a rename visible in.
"""
```

```python
# src/usher/api/routers/home.py
"""`GET /home` -- ADR-0006's route, and the first client-facing one since M5.

**Why a route at all, when M6 and three milestones before it declined one.**
The default in this project is CLI-only: M6 built `SearchService`,
`PostgresSearchIndex`, RRF fusion and the ranking blend and added no HTTP
route, because `usher search` prints exactly what the route would return.
Composition is the first capability where that stops being true. ADR-0006's
central claim -- "One request paints a screen, which is what makes the home
screen feel instant over a slow link" -- is a property of a *request
boundary*, and no CLI can exhibit it. The command still ships (`usher home`),
because PRD 08 requires every operator command to work against an empty
database and a route is a poor place to discover that composition divides by
zero on a household that has watched nothing -- but here the CLI is the
proxy and the route is the deliverable, which is the reverse of M6.

`row.invalidated` is the other half: PRD 07's SSE table assigns it to M7 by
name, and `ports/events.py` says the member is absent "because nothing
composes a row until M7". An invalidation event with no row to invalidate is
an event with no consumer.

**This route cannot fail because a source is down**, and that is structural
rather than defensive: nothing on this path holds a `SourceAdapter`, so
there is no call to catch. PRD 08: "a degraded subsystem narrows
functionality; it never fails a request local state can answer." Every input
is local -- watch state, media items, `title_neighbors`, `user_taste`,
`genome_scores`, credits -- and PRD 08's degradation table already says "LLM
call fails -> Home composes without them". So there is no 503 here, which is
why M5's deferral of PRD 07's RFC 9457 envelope survives this milestone
intact: the envelope's own worked example is `503 source_unavailable`, and
this route has none to give a `code` to. `POST /titles/{id}/play` is still
the named trigger, in M9.

**An empty screen is a 200 with no rows.** Not a 404 -- `/home` is a screen
rather than a resource, and a screen with nothing on it is a fact about the
household. And deliberately not padded with a generic row: a "popular
titles" fallback on a household that has watched nothing produces a screen
that *looks* personalised and is not, which is the failure this milestone
exists to refuse. `rows: []` is distinguishable; a generic row is not.

**Still M9's, so this is a route and not a land grab:** the RFC 9457
envelope, `usher.http.server.duration`, `usher.cache.hits`/`.misses`, HTTP
cache headers, and pagination.
"""

router = APIRouter(tags=["home"])


@router.get("/home", response_model=HomeResponse)
async def get_home(home: HomeServiceDep, user_id: DefaultUserIdDep) -> HomeResponse:
    return HomeResponse.of(await home.compose_for(user_id))
```

`deps.py` gains the repositories groups B/E/F/G landed, a `get_row_context`,
a `get_home_cache` (off `app.state`, same defensive `getattr`/`cast` shape as
`get_event_bus`) and `get_home_service`/`HomeServiceDep` — **each declared
above its first user**, because `Depends(...)` is evaluated when the `def`
below it executes and appending a provider after its consumer is a `NameError`
at import of `usher.api.deps`. `create_app` gains
`app.include_router(home.router)`.

```bash
property of a request boundary and is not observable through a CLI at all,
which is the first time that has been true: usher search prints exactly what
its route would return, and usher home is a proxy for this one.

No cursor: ADR-0006 composes a screen and PRD 07's table gives /browse a
cursor and /home none. No artwork on a card, absent rather than null, for
the sentence M5 wrote one route over -- an always-null field is a branch a
client never takes the other arm of.

An empty database answers 200 with no rows. Not a 404, and deliberately not
padded: a popular-titles fallback on a household that has watched nothing is
a screen that looks personalised and is not."
```

**No `Co-Authored-By`, no `Claude-Session`, no attribution trailer of any
kind.** Verify with `git log -1 --pretty='%(trailers)'`.

## Task 33: `row.invalidated`, in both enums and the wire map

PRD 07's SSE table has held a row for this since M5, assigned to M7 by name:

| Event | Payload | Client action | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `row.invalidated` | Row slug | Refetch that row | M7 |

And `ports/events.py`'s own docstring says why the member is absent today:

> `row.invalidated` is absent because nothing composes a row until M7, and
> `bootstrap.progress` because bootstrap runs in the CLI process while M5's
> bus is in-process. PRD 10's argument for keeping its metric catalogue
> honest applies harder here: an empty dashboard panel is a puzzle, and an
> SSE event type nothing emits is a client handler that waits forever.

That sentence is the whole obligation. M7 composes rows, so the reason for the
absence is gone — and the same rule binds the other direction, which is why
this task lands the member and its publisher in one commit. **A member added
without a publisher is the client handler that waits forever; a publisher
added without a member is a `KeyError` mid-response.**

**Three places move, or the guard fires.**

1. `ClientEventKind.ROW_INVALIDATED = "row.invalidated"` in `ports/events.py`
   — the internal vocabulary, and the docstring's sentence about the absence
   is replaced rather than left to read falsely.
2. `SseEventKind.ROW_INVALIDATED = "row.invalidated"` in `api/dto/events.py`
   — the wire vocabulary, versioned independently, *"with no member nothing
   emits"*.
3. The `_WIRE` mapping, which is documented as:

   > Exhaustive by construction rather than by convention: an internal kind
   > with no wire name is a `KeyError` raised in the middle of a response that
   > already answered 200, where there is no status code left to report it
   > with.

**And "by construction" is currently doing less work than it claims — that is
a finding this task fixes.** `_WIRE` is a plain `dict[ClientEventKind,
SseEventKind]` literal, and **mypy does not check a dict literal for
exhaustiveness over its key enum**. The shipped guard,
`test_the_wire_vocabulary_is_its_own_enum`, asserts the *values of
`SseEventKind`* — so adding the member to **both enums** and forgetting the
`_WIRE` entry passes it, passes mypy, passes the whole suite, and raises
`KeyError` in the middle of a 200 the first time a row is invalidated in
production. So this task adds the case that makes the docstring true:

```python
def test_every_client_event_kind_has_a_wire_name() -> None:
    assert set(_WIRE) == set(ClientEventKind)
```

**The subscription filter cannot express this event, and the settlement is
that it does not have to.**

PRD 07: *"Subscriptions are scoped by query (`?titles=id1,id2`) so a detail
screen isn't woken by unrelated churn."* `_Subscriber.wants` returns `True`
only when `event.title_id is not None and event.title_id in self.titles`. A
`row.invalidated` carries a **row slug** and no title id, so under the shipped
code it reaches **every unfiltered subscriber and no filtered one** — never
"some".

The two candidate answers:

- **A — leave it exactly as it is.** Unfiltered subscribers receive it;
  `?titles=` subscribers do not. **This is the answer**, and the tell that it
  is right is that `_Subscriber.wants` needs **no change at all**. PRD 07's own
  justification for the filter already decides it: a client that sent
  `?titles=` is on a **detail screen**, and a row invalidation is churn for a
  screen that renders no rows. A home client subscribes unfiltered, because it
  renders the whole screen and has no title ids to scope to before it fetches
  one. The filter is doing precisely the job it was written for.
- **B — make `row.invalidated` bypass the filter and reach everyone.** This
  wakes every open detail screen for a row it does not render, which is the
  exact churn the filter exists to prevent, in exchange for nothing: the
  detail screen's response to a row invalidation would be to ignore it.

So: **A, with no code change to the filter, and the consequence documented on
both the route and PRD 07 — a client that wants row invalidations must not
send `?titles=`.** That is a real constraint and it is written down rather
than left for a client author to discover by not receiving events.

The additive change that would relax it is **named and not built**: a `?rows=`
filter, scoping by slug. No client asks for one, v1's only row-rendering
client is the home screen and it wants all of them, and a filter nothing sends
is the `search_queries` failure — a shape fixed before anything has tried to
use it.

**Who publishes it — trap 5 again, and the answer is Task 31's call site.**

> Invalidation must be driven by the **push** lane and by demand reads, not by
> the merge path, or M7 reintroduces the exact fan-out M5 refused.

- **`PushApplyService` publishes**, at the same point where Task 31 calls
  `RowCache.invalidate` and where M5 already publishes `title.updated` and
  `watchstate.updated` — because *"a push event is a change"*. One
  `row.invalidated` per invalidated **slug**, and the slug set is small and
  fixed (the rows a watch state can move), so the fan-out is per *event*, not
  per merged row.
- **The nightly walk publishes none**, exactly as it publishes no
  `watchstate.updated`, and PRD 07's existing sentence covers both without
  amendment: *"a walk merges up to 1,126,789 states, and one … per merged row
  is a fan-out per row per night to every connected client."* With
  `row.invalidated` attached, every one of those messages would also tell every
  client to refetch a row — a fan-out **and** a thundering herd of refetches at
  04:00.
- **The composed screen gets no event of its own.** PRD 07's payload is a *row
  slug* and its client action is *"Refetch that row"*; there is no client
  action for "the server's screen cache expired", and the screen's TTL is a
  server-side cost control rather than a client contract.
- **`EnrichService` publishes none either, and that is a decline rather than an
  omission.** An enrichment changes a *card's contents*, and `title.updated`
  already tells the client to patch that card in place. A second event for the
  same change is a duplicate with no consumer — and at the enriched tier's
  2k–10k titles it is a second fan-out for a screen that does not need
  refetching.

**SSE cannot be tested with `httpx.ASGITransport`, at all, and the failure is a
hang rather than an error.** Its `handle_async_request` runs
`await self.app(scope, receive, send)` **to completion**, collects every
`http.response.body` message, and only then builds a `Response` whose stream
yields `b"".join(body_parts)`. `GET /events` never completes — that is what a
stream is — so `client.stream("GET", "/events")` blocks forever inside the
transport and **no case in the file would ever run**. The M5 plan's own draft
of `tests/unit/test_api_events.py` was written against it and could not have
passed. Every case below uses `tests/fakes/streaming_asgi_transport.py`, whose
scope carries `spec_version: "2.3"` deliberately: `StreamingResponse.__call__`
takes the `listen_for_disconnect` path below 2.4 and a bare `stream_response`
at or above it, and only the first cancels the body iterator when a client goes
away.

**Files:**
- Modify: `src/usher/ports/events.py`, `src/usher/api/dto/events.py`,
  `src/usher/services/push.py`
- Modify: `tests/unit/test_api_dto_events.py`, `tests/unit/test_api_events.py`,
  `tests/unit/test_services_push.py`, `docs/prd/07-client-api.md`

```python
    instruction with no object. Kills an event published with an empty

    """A row is not a title. `title_id` on this event would be a filter key
    that half-works -- it would wake exactly the detail screens subscribed to
    whichever title happened to be attached, which is neither "every
    subscriber" nor "the right ones"."""
    frame = encode_sse(
        _sent(ClientEvent(kind=ClientEventKind.ROW_INVALIDATED, data={"slug": "next-up"}))
    )
    assert "title_id" not in json.loads(frame.split("\n")[2].removeprefix("data: "))
```

```python
# tests/unit/test_api_events.py  (add -- through the streaming transport,
# because `httpx.ASGITransport` runs the app to completion and would hang)

async def test_a_row_invalidation_reaches_an_unfiltered_subscriber(client, bus) -> None:
    """The home client's subscription. It renders the whole screen and has no
    title ids to scope to before it fetches one, so it subscribes
    unfiltered."""
    async with client.stream("GET", "/events") as response:
        lines = aiter(response.aiter_lines())
        await bus.publish(
            ClientEvent(kind=ClientEventKind.ROW_INVALIDATED, data={"slug": "continue-watching"})
        )
        frame = await asyncio.wait_for(_read_frame(lines), timeout=2.0)
    assert "event: row.invalidated" in frame
    assert "continue-watching" in frame


async def test_a_row_invalidation_does_not_wake_a_detail_screen(client, bus) -> None:
    """**The settlement, asserted rather than assumed.** A row-slug event
    carries no title id, so it reaches every subscriber or none -- there is
    no "some". It reaches none of the filtered ones, and that is correct
    rather than a limitation: PRD 07's own reason for `?titles=` is "so a
    detail screen isn't woken by unrelated churn", and a row invalidation is
    unrelated churn for a screen that renders no rows.

    Kills a well-meant `wants()` special case that lets `ROW_INVALIDATED`
    bypass the filter -- which wakes every open detail screen for a row it
    does not render, in exchange for a refetch the client would ignore.
    """
    watched = uuid.uuid4()
    async with client.stream("GET", f"/events?titles={watched}") as response:
        lines = aiter(response.aiter_lines())
        await bus.publish(
            ClientEvent(kind=ClientEventKind.ROW_INVALIDATED, data={"slug": "next-up"})
        )
        await bus.publish(ClientEvent(kind=ClientEventKind.TITLE_UPDATED, title_id=watched))
        frame = await asyncio.wait_for(_read_frame(lines), timeout=2.0)
    assert "row.invalidated" not in frame
    assert str(watched) in frame
```

```python
# src/usher/ports/events.py
class ClientEventKind(StrEnum):
    """PRD 07's SSE table, restricted to what this process emits.

    `bootstrap.progress` is absent because bootstrap runs in the CLI process
    while the bus is in-process, so there is no channel from one to the
    other. PRD 10's argument for keeping its metric catalogue honest applies
    harder here: an empty dashboard panel is a puzzle, and an SSE event type
    nothing emits is a client handler that waits forever.

    **`row.invalidated` landed with M7**, which is the milestone that
    composes a row -- and it landed in the same commit as its publisher, for
    the reason above pointed the other way.
    """

    TITLE_UPDATED = "title.updated"
    WATCHSTATE_UPDATED = "watchstate.updated"
    # Payload is a **row slug**, and deliberately no `title_id`: a row is not
    # a title. This is therefore the one event the `?titles=` filter cannot
    # express -- it reaches unfiltered subscribers and no others, which is
    # correct rather than a limitation. A client that sent `?titles=` is on a
    # detail screen, and PRD 07's own reason for the filter is "so a detail
    # screen isn't woken by unrelated churn".
    ROW_INVALIDATED = "row.invalidated"
    SYNC_PROGRESS = "sync.progress"
    RESYNC_REQUIRED = "resync_required"
```

convention.

data={"slug": slug})` per slug it invalidated, at Task 31's call site.
`WatchStateSyncService` gains nothing, and the comment Task 31 put there names

## Task 34: `usher home`, and the composition measured rather than asserted

The command ships alongside the route rather than instead of it, and PRD 08
says why: *"every one of them has to work against an empty database"*, and a
route is a poor place to find out that composition divides by zero on a
household that has watched nothing. It is also where boundary call 8's promise
is kept — **"Task 34 measures it; the plan does not assert it."**

**Shape, following `usher similar` exactly.** A parser entry in `_parser()`, a
private async coroutine `_home(...)`, an arm in `main`'s command chain, and
**`print` throughout, never `logger`** — the same split every command in this
module makes: `loguru` output is operational and goes to a log sink, and a
command's answer is stdout an operator reads or pipes.

```python
home = sub.add_parser("home", help="compose the home screen, and time it")
home.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=10)
home.add_argument("--repeat", type=int, default=1)
```

**Cross-argument rule: there is none, and that is stated rather than
omitted.** `usher similar` needed one (`bool(args.title_id) == bool(args.rebuild)`)
because its two arguments select between two *different operations*, one of
which writes the whole neighbour table. `usher home` has one operation and two
scalars; the only validation is `--limit >= 1` and `--repeat >= 1`, which go
beside the identical checks `search` and `suggest` already have in
`parse_args`. Recorded because a reader comparing this command to its template
will look for the rule and should find the reason it is absent.

**It must work against an empty database**, and that is a case rather than a
hope. The failure it is hunting is arithmetic, not a missing row: **the taste
centroid is a mean, and the mean of zero embeddings is `0/0`.** Group G owns
`TasteService`, but `usher home` is where an operator meets it, and PRD 08's
rule exists because this is exactly the class of thing that ships. Against an
empty database the command prints a report in which every provider proposed
nothing, zero rows were built, and the exit status is **0** — because an empty
household is a fact, not an error.

**The report shape for an operator.** One line per provider, and **a provider
that proposed nothing gets a line reading `0`, never omission** — an absent
provider and a silent one are the two states this whole milestone exists to
distinguish, and a report that drops the silent ones makes them
indistinguishable from unregistered ones.

```
provider              proposed  built  cards   propose     build
continue-watching            1      1     12     3.1 ms    18.4 ms
next-up                      1      1      8     5.6 ms    22.0 ms
recently-added               1      1     20     1.2 ms    11.9 ms
because-you-watched          3      2     24    14.8 ms    61.2 ms
franchise                    0      -      -     2.0 ms         -
genre-affinity               1      0      0     9.4 ms     7.7 ms
seasonal                     0      -      -     0.3 ms         -
people                       2      2     16    11.1 ms    43.5 ms
rediscover                   0      -      -     4.2 ms         -

9 providers, 4 proposed nothing, 1 built empty and was dropped
screen: 7 rows, 80 cards
compose (cold)  198.4 ms      compose (warm, from cache)  0.3 ms
```

Three columns are doing specific work. `proposed 0` is a provider with nothing
to say. `built 0` on a row that proposed is a row **dropped** — the state PRD
06's "drops any that build empty" produces, and the only place in the system it
is visible. And the cold/warm pair is the **only measurement of the cache this
milestone has**, because `usher.cache.hits`/`.misses` is M9's (Task 31).

**What is measured, and at what scale.**

- `usher.home.compose.duration` for the whole composition, and the per-provider
  `usher.row.build.duration` breakdown — **the two metrics PRD 10 assigns to
  M7 and nothing else** (Task 30). The per-provider **propose** time is
  printed in the report and is **not** a metric: PRD 10 assigns two, and a
  third under a name no dashboard reads is the empty-panel failure in advance.
- `--repeat N` measures N **cold** compositions, clearing the cache before
  each, then one warm read. A repeat that measured cache hits would report a
  number near zero and mean nothing.
- **Scale, with the synthetic parts named**, because this plan's discipline is
  that a measurement states its denominator:
  - **catalog** — a full `usher bootstrap` (1,271,138 titles), which is the
    population every provider's query filters against;
  - **library** — the bounded live ingest the M4/M5 live runs use, which is the
    only real `media_items` and `episodes` data available;
  - **watch state** — **synthetic and said so.** A real household's watch
    history cannot be manufactured by a live run, so the measurement seeds a
    realistic one: an enriched tier of 2k–10k titles and a few hundred
    `watch_states` rows spread over two years, which is what makes
    `ContinueWatching`, `NextUp`, `BecauseYouWatched`, `GenreAffinity` and
    `Rediscover` fire at all. Every one of those providers returns nothing on
    the live data alone, so a measurement without seeded watch state would
    time **four** providers and report the sequential build as free.

**The threshold — the number that would make M9 revisit the sequential
build.** A boundary call that promises a measurement and does not name the
threshold is a boundary call nobody can act on, so the plan names **two
numbers and a rule that combines them**:

1. **Budget — `usher.home.compose.duration` p95 > 400 ms.** ADR-0006's claim
   is *"One request paints a screen, which is what makes the home screen feel
   instant over a slow link"*, and the perceived-instant budget for a screen
   paint is ~1 s end to end. 400 ms of server time leaves ~600 ms for the
   network and the client render, which is the half of that budget Usher does
   not control. Below 400 ms the sequential build is not the problem, whatever
   else is. M6's 50 ms p95 is deliberately **not** reused: that is a keystroke
   budget for as-you-type suggest, and applying it to a screen paint would
   condemn the sequential build against a bar nothing in the design promised.
2. **Shape — the slowest single provider is ≥ 50% of the total build time.**
   This is the condition under which **concurrency is the wrong lever**. If one
   provider is most of the wall clock, parallelising nine of them converges on
   that one provider's latency and buys nothing; the finding is a query to fix,
   and M9 fixes the query.

**Combined, the rule is:**

> **Revisit the sequential build only when p95 > 400 ms *and* no single
> provider accounts for ≥ 50% of the total.** Over budget with a dominant
> provider is a **query** to fix. Under budget is neither.

And the third number, because the rule has to say what "revisit" means: **if
both conditions hold, the redesign is a session per row behind a bounded pool
— i.e. a lane — and PRD 01's concurrency table grows a row, which is precisely
what boundary call 8 says does not exist today** (*"a semaphore has no lane to
belong to"*). That is actionable: it names the trigger, the lever, and the
document that must change with it.

The measured per-provider table is recorded in the milestone verification
task's report, so PRD 10's dashboard 4 has an expected shape to draw against
rather than an empty panel with no baseline.

## Task 35: The tag genome becomes `SimilarityService`'s fourth signal, and invalidates every neighbour row already stored

`services/similar.py`'s own module docstring makes a promise, and this is the milestone that cashes it in:

> So the blend is a **sum of weighted terms over an explicit signal list**, and landing a third signal is one `_WEIGHTS` entry, one accessor and one case -- not a rewritten scorer.

PRD 09's tag-genome paragraph repeats it (*"one weighted term in `SimilarityService`'s existing signal list"*), and the "What M7 inherits" table in `docs/plans/progress.md` repeats it a third time. **Check it rather than repeat it, because it is slightly optimistic and correcting it is worth more than quoting it.**

`_blend` really is one entry and one kwarg — `_blend(**signals: float | None)` iterates `_WEIGHTS`, so `tags=…` at the call site in `_neighbors_for` is the whole of the scorer change, and that half of the promise is exactly true. What the docstring does not account for is where the signal *comes from*. `NeighborSeed` and `NeighborCandidate` are `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)` and they live in **`ports/repository.py:1124-1155`**, not in `services/`; they carry `genres`/`keywords` because M6's two Jaccard terms needed them, and a fourth signal needs a fourth field on a **port DTO** — which is a contract-suite change and a fake change, not a service change. And the values are filled by two SQL constants in `db/repositories/search.py`: `_LIST_EMBEDDED` (the seed page) and `_NEAREST` (the pairwise candidate pool).

**So the real cost is one `_WEIGHTS` entry, one accessor, two DTO fields on a port, two widened statements, both fakes, and the contract suite — and PRD 05's and PRD 09's sentences are corrected to say so in this task's commit.** The promise's *spirit* holds — nothing about the scorer is rewritten, `_blend` is untouched, and no consumer of `title_neighbors` changes — and saying that precisely is more useful than either defending the sentence or deleting it.

- Modify: `src/usher/db/repositories/search.py` (`_LIST_EMBEDDED`, `_NEAREST`)

- [ ] **Step 1: Measure the genome cosine's spread before choosing its weight — the term may be structurally inert**

**This step runs first and it can cancel the rest of the task.** Every component of a genome vector is a relevance in `[0.00024999999999997247, 1.0]` with mean **0.1111** (the front matter counted it). A cosine between two vectors with no negative components is bounded below by 0 — it *cannot* be negative, unlike the embedding cosine, which genuinely can — and, worse, two vectors that share a common background profile score high on each other whatever they are about. This is the saturation failure `_WEIGHTS`' own comment already names for genres:

> `genres` 0.15: a guard, not a driver […] Smallest because it *saturates*: a closed set of roughly nineteen values with two to four per title means any two dramas score 0.33 or better against each other regardless of subject.

**A 1,128-dimension dense non-negative matrix is a candidate for exactly that, at a much larger weight.** So measure it the way this project has measured every other signal's non-vacuity — `FakeEmbedder`'s off-diagonal cosine (mean −0.00001, **sd 0.05102** against a theoretical 1/√384 = 0.05103), and the name-only-skeleton control (pairwise **0.5867, sd 0.055**, against a skeleton retrieving its own enriched form at 0.7638 and a 0.4751 cross-title mean). Same shape, from a throwaway script outside the working tree, against the real `genome_scores` group F loads:

- **The off-diagonal distribution** over a random sample of pairs (5,000 pairs is ample at 16,376 rows): mean, sd, min, max, and the 5th/50th/95th percentiles.
- **A planted control**, so the number means something: a known sequel pair or a known franchise pair against a known unrelated pair. Synthetic titles cannot produce this — the genome is real data — so the control is *two real `movieId`s named by their genome row, never by their title*, and neither the ids nor the names are written into the repository. Report it as "a same-franchise pair scored X against a cross-genre pair at Y".
- **The same two statistics after mean-centering** — i.e. over `v − mean(v)` across the 16,376 rows.

**The bar, written down here before the number is known:** if the off-diagonal **sd is below 0.05**, the term is saturated and at weight 0.25 it can move a blended score by at most ~0.0125 — *less than the 0.0167 the re-weighting itself moves every pair that has no genome at all* (Step 2's arithmetic). A term that perturbs less than its own introduction is decoration, and landing it would be adding a `<=>` and a TOAST fetch to every candidate pair of every rebuild to buy ordering noise.

**If it saturates, the answer is centering, not abandonment.** Store `v − mean(v)` in `genome_scores` — the mean vector is one row, computed once at import, `halfvec` carries negatives without complaint, and a centered cosine is the standard fix for a matrix with a strong common component. That is a change to group F's importer, so if this step reaches that conclusion the task **stops, records the number, and hands the correction back** rather than papering over it with a smaller weight. Record the decision either way; a measurement that only gets written down when it agrees with the plan is not a measurement.

- [ ] **Step 2: The weight — and the arithmetic that bounds what re-weighting can break**

**Re-weighting is the decision. The addition is the easy half.** Today:

```python
_WEIGHTS: dict[str, float] = {"cosine": 0.60, "keywords": 0.25, "genres": 0.15}
```

Adding a fourth entry moves all three of the others, and `_blend` renormalises over *present* signals — so a title with a genome vector and a title without are scored on **different denominators**. That is the design, deliberately (`_blend`'s own docstring: *"an absent signal leaves the numerator and the denominator"*, because dividing by `sum(_WEIGHTS.values())` unconditionally would score an untagged pair at 0.60× its true cosine agreement). It is also precisely what makes "did the weights change the ordering" hard to see, because the two populations are not comparable by construction.

**The weight this plan proposes, and the reason it is this number and not a round one:**

```python
_WEIGHTS: dict[str, float] = {"cosine": 0.45, "tags": 0.25, "keywords": 0.20, "genres": 0.10}
```

| Term | Was | Now | Renormalised when `tags` is absent |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cosine` | 0.60 | 0.45 | 0.45 / 0.75 = **0.600** |
| `keywords` | 0.25 | 0.20 | 0.20 / 0.75 = **0.267** |
| `genres` | 0.15 | 0.10 | 0.10 / 0.75 = **0.133** |
| `tags` | — | 0.25 | absent |

**The three chosen numbers sum to 0.75, and that is the whole argument.** On every pair with no genome — which on the catalog is 98.2% of them and on the enriched tier is whatever Task 36 measures — the renormalised cosine share is **exactly 0.600, unchanged to three decimal places**, and keywords and genres move by **+0.0167 and −0.0167**. The score of a no-genome pair therefore moves by `0.0167 × (keywords − genres)`, which is bounded by **±0.0167**, and two such pairs can only swap if they were already within **0.033** of each other. State it that way rather than claiming the ordering is preserved: it mostly is, the bound is arithmetic, and the residual is real.

`tags` at 0.25 — the same weight keywords used to carry — because it is the same *kind* of claim (a topical vocabulary over the work's content) made better: 1,128 dimensions of human-scored relevance against a sparse editorial keyword list, dense where keywords are long-tail. It does not go higher than `cosine` because cosine is the only term computed over the actual prose and the only one present on *every* embedded pair. It does not go lower than `keywords` because if a human-scored 1,128-dimension relevance vector is worth less than a keyword set, it is not worth landing.

**And it is chosen with an argument, not measured.** Nothing in this project measures similarity relevance — M6 said that out loud in `_WEIGHTS`' own comment and in PRD 05, and M7 does not change it. Step 1 measures the signal's *spread*, which is a property of the data and decides whether the term is inert; it says nothing about whether 0.25 is better than 0.20. Keep the two claims separate in the comment, in the PRD and in the ADR amendment. A weight with a measurement next to it that measures something else is worse than a weight with no measurement at all.

**The weights stay constants and the settings block stays unamended**, for the reason already recorded in `similar.py`:

> A weight is not an operator knob: changing it changes what "similar" means, and every row of the precomputed artefact was written under the old meaning.

That sentence is now this task's own problem — see Step 5.

- [ ] **Step 3: Two DTO fields, two widened statements, and `None` where a vector is missing**

`NeighborCandidate` gains **`tags: float | None`** — a **cosine, never a distance**, for the reason its sibling field already carries in its docstring (*"pgvector's `<=>` is a distance and the blend wants agreement, so `1 - (a <=> b)` happens once, in the adapter"*). `None` when **either** side has no `genome_scores` row. Not `0.0`: [ADR-0014](../prd/decisions/0014-absence-is-not-zero.md) again, and this is the case that catches the difference —

> **A pair where one side has a genome vector and the other does not is `None`, not a cosine against nothing.** `0.0` says "these two films share no tags", which for a genome vector is a claim no pair can actually make (every component is positive, so the true cosine of any real pair is well above zero). It would be the single most confident *wrong* statement in the blend: a genome-bearing title's neighbours would be reordered to put every other genome-bearing title above every un-genomed one, and at 1.8% catalog coverage that is a 1.8% clique pinned to the top of 98.2% of the lists.

`NeighborSeed` gains **`has_genome: bool`**. It is not read by `_blend`; it is read by the rebuild, which counts it, so that "what fraction of the seeds this rebuild processed carried a genome vector" is a number the rebuild reports rather than a second query somebody has to think to run. That is the coverage figure Task 36 needs and PRD 05 has never had, arriving from the code path that consumes it.

**Two widened statements, and the pairwise one is `_NEAREST` rather than `_TAGS_FOR`.** `_TAGS_FOR` (`SELECT id, genres, keywords FROM titles WHERE id = ANY(:title_ids)`) is *per candidate*; the genome cosine is *per pair*, so it cannot come from there. It goes on `_NEAREST`, which is already the pairwise statement and already returns exactly the pair set the blend needs:

- `_LIST_EMBEDDED` gains `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM genome_scores g WHERE g.title_id = e.title_id) AS has_genome`.
- `_NEAREST` gains a `LEFT JOIN genome_scores` on each side of the lateral and `1 - (gs.vector <=> gc.vector) AS tags`, `NULL` when either join misses.

**Not a third statement**, which is the obvious alternative: a third round trip per page, over a pair set `_NEAREST` has already materialised, for a value the same query can produce. Say that in the comment next to the join, in the shape `_NEAREST`'s existing three-clause comment is written.

Both fakes mirror the `None`-when-either-side-is-missing rule. **The fake must not be strengthened past that** — the standing rule from M3's live run (40 contract assertions green against a write-back that had never once worked) and from `_neighbors_for`'s own kept self-guard.

- [ ] **Step 4: The cases, each asserting on position and each seeding the distractor**

M6's rule, inherited and tightened by this milestone's front matter: *every provider case asserts on position, and seeds a distractor a broken implementation would rank first.* It applies here too, because `title_neighbors` is what three of M7's providers read.

| Case | The wrong implementation it kills | The distractor it seeds |
|---|---|---|
| `test_a_genome_pair_outranks_an_equally_close_pair_without_one` | the fourth term never reaching `_blend` | a candidate with a marginally *higher* embedding cosine and no genome row — so a membership assertion, and a cosine-only scorer, both pass |
| `test_a_pair_with_one_genome_vector_scores_None_not_zero` | `tags=0.0` on a half-missing pair | a third candidate with *both* sides genomed at a mediocre cosine, which a `0.0` implementation ranks below the half-missing pair and a correct one ranks above |
| `test_a_pair_with_no_genome_is_scored_within_two_hundredths_of_the_m6_blend` | a re-weighting that quietly moved the un-genomed 98% | the M6 weights computed inline in the case, asserted `abs(new - old) <= 0.0167` — the arithmetic bound from Step 2, pinned rather than described |
| `test_the_genome_term_is_clamped_to_the_unit_interval` | an unclamped term breaking `CHECK (score >= 0 AND score <= 1)` | a hand-planted negative `tags`, which real data cannot produce and a port implementation can |
| `test_the_rebuild_reports_how_many_seeds_carried_a_genome` | `has_genome` filled but never counted | a page of five seeds, two genomed |

The third of those is the one worth writing carefully. It is the only case that can see the *re-weighting* rather than the *addition*, and a plan that ships a four-way blend with no case pinning what happened to the three-way one has changed the meaning of every stored row for a population it never tested.

**Each new case's docstring names the wrong implementation it rules out**, per the front matter's rule 3.

- [ ] **Step 5: `title_neighbors` has no fingerprint, so every row already stored is now wrong and nothing can tell the halves apart**

This is the part of the task that is not about the genome at all.

M6 shipped this table with a whole-artefact `computed_at()` and no fingerprint, and wrote the gap down honestly rather than dressing it up — `similar.py`'s docstring calls it *"the milestone's one acknowledged gap"*, and `docs/plans/progress.md` lists **"no automatic `title_neighbors` refresh — the milestone's one honest freshness gap"** among what M7 does not get. The reason is real and it does not go away: a neighbour row goes stale when *some other* title gets an embedding, which no per-row predicate can decide.

**M7 makes that gap strictly worse, in a way M6's reasoning does not cover.** Step 2 changes what a stored `score` *means*. Every row written before this task was computed under a three-signal blend at different weights; every row written after is a four-signal blend. Both are in the same table, both are in `[0, 1]`, both have a plausible `rank`, and **nothing distinguishes them**. A full `usher similar --rebuild` is the only remedy, and **nothing schedules it** — the CLI section of `CLAUDE.md` says so in as many words: *"Nothing runs `usher similar --rebuild` for you."*

**So M7 goes further than a release note, and the argument for going further is that this is exactly the state [ADR-0020](../prd/decisions/0020-derived-state-carries-its-fingerprint.md) exists to eliminate**, quoted from its own Decision section:

> **Nothing in this milestone infers freshness. Every derived artefact is either fresh by construction, or carries the fingerprint of the input it was derived from so that staleness is a query.**

`title_neighbors` was the one artefact M6 exempted, on the grounds that the input it derives from is *the whole other table* and cannot be fingerprinted per row. That argument is correct about one of the two staleness causes and silent about the other. **M7 closes the one it can:**

- **`title_neighbors.blend_fingerprint text NOT NULL`**, an `md5` of the canonical serialisation of `_WEIGHTS` (sorted keys), `_NEIGHBORS_PER_TITLE` and `_CANDIDATE_POOL` — the three constants that between them define what a stored score means. One column, one module-level function, one predicate.
- **`usher similar <title id>` compares the stored fingerprint against the running one and says so when they differ**, in the shape `--mode fused` narrows rather than fails: it still prints the neighbours, and it prints *"these neighbours were computed under a different blend; run `usher similar --rebuild`"*. Narrowed, not broken; PRD 08's degradation rule.
- **`usher.similarity.neighbors.stale` gauge**, a `count(*)` over rows whose fingerprint is not the current one, fed by the same predicate — one definition, three consumers, which is ADR-0020's argument in one metric and is exactly the shape `usher.search.embeddings.stale` already has.
- **`usher similar --rebuild` writes the current fingerprint and, at the end, logs the coverage counter from Step 3.**

**What this does not close, stated rather than implied.** The fingerprint answers *"was this row computed under the current meaning?"* It does **not** answer *"has some other title been embedded since?"* — that half is genuinely undecidable per row and M7 leaves it exactly where M6 left it, with the operator or a cron entry. Two staleness causes, one closed, and saying which is the difference between an improvement and a claim.

**Rejected, with reasons, because each is the tempting answer:**

| Rejected | Why |
|---|---|
| Document the rebuild in the release note and stop | M6 already named this gap; a milestone that *widens* a named gap and re-names it has documented drift rather than prevented it |
| Truncate `title_neighbors` in the migration | An empty table and a stale table are both wrong, and the empty one is worse: `SimilarityRow` renders nothing, `computed_at()` returns `None`, and an operator who does not read the release note sees a feature that regressed rather than one that is out of date |
| A `similar` job kind that self-schedules on embedding change | It needs the trigger M6 proved undecidable. A job kind whose enqueue predicate cannot be written is a queue that either never fires or fires per embedded title, and the second is a full rebuild per enriched title |
| Make `_WEIGHTS` a `Settings` field so a deployment can keep the old blend | Explicitly refused by `similar.py`'s existing comment, and it produces the exact table-half-computed-under-each-definition state this column exists to detect |

**This column is a fifth migration and the plan says four.** The genome migration belongs to group F, which runs before this group in the serial order, so amending it in place is not available. Ship the fifth, name it in its own docstring as the blend-fingerprint migration, and **Task 38 records it as a planned fifth rather than a surprise** — the front matter's rule is that a fifth is a *finding*, not that it is forbidden, and a finding recorded in advance with its reason is what that rule is for.

- [ ] **Step 6: The candidate pool is chosen by cosine alone, so the genome term may have almost nothing to promote**

`_CANDIDATE_POOL = 100`, and the pool comes out of `_NEAREST` ordered by embedding distance. Its comment explains why it is larger than what is stored:

> Larger than what is stored, because the blend reorders: a candidate ranked 40th on cosine alone can enter the stored 25 on tag overlap, and a pool equal to the output leaves the tag terms unable to promote anything -- decoration on a pure cosine ranking.

**That argument is about coverage the genome does not have.** Genres and keywords are on essentially every enriched title, so the pool is full of candidates the tag terms can move. The genome is on 16,376 movies — **1.82% of the catalog's movies** — so if genome membership were independent of pool membership, a genome-bearing seed's pool of 100 would hold about **two** genome-bearing candidates, and a term that can reorder two candidates out of a hundred is decoration whatever its weight.

It is *not* independent — both genome membership and pool membership correlate hard with popularity and with enrichment — which is why the number that matters is the **pair** rate on the enriched tier and not the square of the title rate. **Task 36 measures it.** This task states the mechanism, writes the counter that produces the number (Step 3's `has_genome`, plus a second counter for how many of each seed's 100 candidates carried a `tags` value), and does **not** widen the pool on a guess. If Task 36 comes back below the bar it writes down, the two honest answers are a genome-aware pool for genome-bearing seeds or dropping the term and reverting the weights — and both are decisions for the measurement to make, not for this task.

The bullet reading *"⏳ MovieLens tag-genome cosine where available (~7% coverage, weighted in only when present) — **the importer does not exist**"* loses its ⏳ and gains the shipped weight, the real denominators from the front matter (1.82% of movies / 1.29% of all titles / 8.7% of the ~189k priority tier), and a pointer to Task 36 for the enriched-tier figure. The paragraph naming the shipped `(0.60 / 0.25 / 0.15)` split is replaced with the new one **and the renormalisation arithmetic from Step 2**, because that is what tells a reader what happened to the catalog they already have.
- **PRD 05 and PRD 09** — the "one entry and one accessor" sentence is corrected in both, to the accounting at the top of this task. It is one entry and one accessor *in the scorer*, plus two port DTO fields, two statements, two fakes and a contract suite.
- **PRD 09's tag-genome paragraph** — its "what it costs" list said *"one weighted term in `SimilarityService`'s existing signal list"*. Same correction, and it gains what the term cost in invalidation, which was not on the list at all.
- **[ADR-0020](../prd/decisions/0020-derived-state-carries-its-fingerprint.md)** — amended, not superseded, per `.claude/rules/prd-maintenance.md`'s rule that a resolved position is updated with its new evidence. Its **Uncertainty** section already says the fingerprint proves the *text* is current and not the *assembly rule*; M7 is the milestone that proves that concern was live (weight class B moves every fingerprint at once, deliberately) and the milestone that extends the scheme to the one artefact M6 exempted. ## Task 36: The `titles.popularity` re-measure M6 handed over, and the genome-coverage number that has never had a denominator

**This is a measurement task, in the shape of M6's Task 26.** It runs against a real catalog, it writes its bar down *before* it runs, and its deliverable is the recorded result whichever way it goes. It fixes nothing it has not first measured.

M6's gate changed a shipped default on the strength of a number, and then M6's own Task 28 found the finding underneath that number was half wrong. `CLAUDE.md` records the correction and hands the rest here, and it is worth quoting because both halves are load-bearing:

> **"Nothing in `src/` writes that column but TMDb enrichment" was part of this finding and is REFUTED — corrected 2026-08-03 by M6's Task 28.** `PostgresBulkCatalogRepository.link_crosswalk` (`db/repositories/bulk.py:495`) writes `popularity = COALESCE(m.popularity, t.popularity)` from `tmdb_ids`, reached by `usher bootstrap --phase crosswalk|all` (`cli.py:147`), and `ports/repository.py:318` documents that write. […] M2's live run linked **291,737 of 1,271,138** titles, so a full bootstrap leaves roughly **23%** carrying a popularity, most of it on skeletons. **The partially-populated catalog is the case nobody has measured and it is worse than either extreme**: popularity is a *hard* key above `vote_count`, and `tmdb_ids.popularity` is `NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, so a crosswalk-linked skeleton at `0.0` sorts **above** an unlinked title with 500,000 votes — the exact "whichever skeleton the scan reached first" failure `NULLS LAST` is there to prevent, from the other side. The +4.2/+8.3 win was measured where the new key was never contested. M7 owns re-measuring it.

So the gate's catalog was bootstrapped IMDb-phase-only, the shipped default was tuned on a catalog where the key above it was inert, and **the configuration a real operator gets — a `--phase all` bootstrap — has never been measured at all.**

**Files:**
- Modify: `src/usher/adapters/search/postgres.py` (the comment at 743–765, and the `ORDER BY` if the measurement says so)
- Modify: `src/usher/ports/repository.py:318-320` (the `ix_titles_popularity` justification)
- Modify: `src/usher/services/search.py` (`SearchService._popularity_term`'s docstring — *"most of 1,271,138 rows"*, which is a bootstrap-only figure stated as a general one)
- Modify: `docs/prd/05-search-and-similarity.md`, `docs/prd/decisions/0002-postgres-first-search.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/plans/progress.md`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the bar down, outside the working tree, before anything runs**

M6's gate did this at `/tmp/m6-gate/BAR.md` and it is the single thing that made a failed gate a closed item rather than an argument. Same here, at `/tmp/m7-gate/BAR.md`, committed to nothing and written before Step 2.

**Bar A — the regression bar for the suggest ordering.** This is not an absolute recall bar; M6 already established that the shipped path fails an absolute bar below 8 characters and that M9 owns the fix. The question here is narrower and answerable: **does making the catalog realistic make it worse?**

> Against the identical 2,993 cases (seed **20260803**, `vote_count ≥ 500`, non-unique names excluded, five equal draws of 150 over bands 2–4 / 5–7 / 8–11 / 12–19 / 20+, four typo classes), the shipped configuration on a `--phase all` catalog must lose **no more than 2.0 points of recall@5 overall** and **no more than 4.0 points on any single length band** against its measured values on the IMDb-only catalog — **82.5% overall, 36.1% on 2–4, 77.5% on 5–7** — and p50 must not move by more than 10% from 33.6 ms.

**Bar B — the remedy bar.** A remedy ships only if it (i) recovers at least the points lost, (ii) costs no more than 10% on p50, and (iii) **does not reduce recall on the all-NULL catalog**, because a deployment can legitimately be in either state and a default that fixes one by breaking the other is not a fix.

**Bar C — the genome-term bar.** Written here because Task 35 Step 6 depends on it:

> If **fewer than 10% of the candidate pairs** that reach `_blend` during a rebuild over a real owned population carry a `tags` value, the genome term at weight 0.25 is decoration and the honest answers are a genome-aware candidate pool or dropping the term and reverting the weights.

**Same seed, same procedure, same code path, or the two numbers are not comparable.** The whole value of this task is a controlled comparison against a measurement that already exists; re-sampling, re-seeding or hand-writing the SQL turns it into a second unrelated number. Query through `PostgresSuggestIndex.suggest(prefix, limit=5)` imported the way the CLI does, through `composition`.

If the implementer disagrees with any of these three numbers, change them **in this document, before running**, with the reasoning.

- [ ] **Step 2: Build the catalog the way an operator does — `--phase all`, three minutes, no API key**

`bootstrap --phase all` reaches IMDb's dumps, TMDb's **public daily id export files** (not the API — no key) and Wikidata's **public SPARQL endpoint**. `CLAUDE.md` records the last full run at **1,271,314 titles, 291,772 with a `tmdb_id`, 539,006 with a community rating, in 2 min 59 s wall clock**.

```bash
cd /home/anirudhlath/code/usher
docker run -d --name usher-m7-gate -e POSTGRES_USER=usher -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=usher \
  -e POSTGRES_DB=usher -p 5433:5432 pgvector/pgvector:pg17

set -a; . ./.env; set +a
export USHER_DATABASE_URL="postgresql+asyncpg://usher:usher@localhost:5433/usher"
uv run alembic upgrade head
uv run usher bootstrap --phase all
uv run usher bootstrap-status
```

`set -a; . ./.env; set +a` rather than a literal value, for the reason `CLAUDE.md`'s Commands section already gives: *"so no credential ever reaches a shell history or a recorded command."* The `USHER_DATABASE_URL` override is a scratch container on 5433 and is deliberately the one thing typed literally — it holds no secret, and pointing a measurement at the same database a dev shell uses is how a measurement quietly becomes a schema change.

**Two hazards this run inherits, both already recorded:**

- **`CachedDatasetFile` is keyed on the upstream token, not on local presence.** M6's gate would have re-downloaded 224 MB of a *different* IMDb snapshot; pinning `revision()` to the sidecar's own value is what made it read the cached bytes, and NIC counters moved 1.2 MB across the whole bootstrap. Do the same, and report the NIC delta, or the run has silently measured a different catalog.
- **Record the counts you get, do not assume the counts above.** IMDb regenerates daily; if the numbers differ, say so and use yours. *"Treat every figure derived from it as a snapshot with a date on it, not a constant."*

Then apply the search schema, exactly as the gate did:

```bash
uv run usher index --backfill --dry-run    # how many titles the stale predicate claims
```

The backfill itself is **not** run — the suggest path is trigram plus `levenshtein_less_equal` over `titles.name` and needs no embedding, and 4–6 hours over 1.27M titles buys nothing this half of the task uses.

- [ ] **Step 3: Measure the distribution of `titles.popularity`, not just the fraction**

**"~23% carrying a popularity, most of it `0.0` on skeletons" is itself an inference and this step settles it.** `tmdb_ids.popularity` being `NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` says what the *column* permits; it does not say what TMDb's daily export actually carries, and the difference is the whole finding. A catalog where 23% carry a *real* popularity is a catalog where the shipped ordering suddenly works as designed on nearly a quarter of it. A catalog where 23% carry `0.0` is the pathology `CLAUDE.md` describes. **These are opposite conclusions and nobody has looked.**

Record all of:

| Quantity | Why it is separate |
|---|---|
| `count(*) WHERE popularity IS NOT NULL` and its fraction | the headline, against the predicted ~23% |
| `count(*) WHERE popularity = 0` and its fraction of the non-NULL set | the pathology's actual size |
| percentiles (p5/p25/p50/p75/p95/max) of the **non-zero** values | whether the signal is real where it exists |
| the same three, split by `enrichment_state` and by `kind` | a skeleton at 0.0 and an enriched title at 14.2 are different populations sharing one key |
| `count(*) WHERE popularity IS NOT NULL AND vote_count IS NULL` | the exact contested set: rows where the hard key fires and the tiebreak has nothing |
| the same for `popularity = 0 AND vote_count >= 500` | the "skeleton at 0.0 outranks a title with 500,000 votes" case, counted |

The last two are the ones that decide Step 5, because they are the rows where the shipped ordering's two keys actually disagree.

**The enriched tier's population is the set of titles a household owns**, and matching produces that set without a single TMDb request — `enrichment_state` is downstream of it. So:


**Bound it in the iterator, never with `max_pages`** — exhausting `max_pages` raises `PortDataMalformed` and records `FAILED`, which is the walk's dead-man's switch and not a bound. |---|---|

| the same over the enriched subset, if the run enriches any | enriched titles |
| **candidate-pair coverage** — of the 100 candidates each genome-bearing seed's pool holds, how many carried a `tags` value | seed × candidate pairs |

> Below a 10% pair rate the term reorders roughly one list in ten and costs a `<=>` plus a TOAST fetch on every candidate pair of every rebuild. At that point the two honest answers are (a) a genome-aware candidate pool — widen `_CANDIDATE_POOL` for genome-bearing seeds, or select part of the pool by genome distance instead of by embedding distance — or (b) drop the term and revert `_WEIGHTS` to M6's three, which costs one commit and one rebuild because Task 35's `blend_fingerprint` makes the revert detectable. Whichever is chosen, PRD 05's coverage bullet carries this measurement and not the ~7%.

Also record the two facts that bound how far this number generalises: the genome is **movies only**, and it is **frozen at 2023-07-20** (`Last-Modified: Thu, 20 Jul 2023 20:20:32 GMT`, unmoved in three years), so coverage of anything released since is structurally zero and will decay. That is not a defect to fix; it is a property of the signal that belongs next to its weight.

## Task 37: The PRD and the ADRs

**This is not a documentation pass at the end of the milestone.** `CLAUDE.md`'s standing rule is unambiguous:

> **Update the PRD in the same commit as the change that invalidates it.** Not in a follow-up, not "later". A change that alters behaviour and leaves the PRD stale is incomplete.

So what follows is a **checklist of what each earlier task owes**, enumerated file by file, so that a reviewer of Task 12 or Task 29 can look up what that task was supposed to have carried with it. Anything still outstanding when this task runs is a task that shipped incomplete, and the fix is to land it here rather than to pretend the rule held.

The ADRs are the genuine exception: an ADR records a decision *and its consequences*, and two of M7's carry evidence that only exists once the thing is built and measured.

**M7 has more of this work than any milestone before it**, for a reason worth stating at the top: it is the first milestone whose *subject document* (PRD 06) was written entirely before any of it existed, and PRD 06 carries **no `⏳` and no `🔶` marker anywhere in the file**. Every one of its statements reads as shipped. Three of them are wrong, one describes a data field that does not exist, and one describes a concurrency model that would corrupt a session. A document with no markers is not a document with no gaps; it is a document nobody has audited, and this task is the audit.

**Files:**
- Modify: `docs/prd/01-architecture.md`, `02-data-model.md`, `03-sources-and-sync.md`, `04-catalog-bootstrap.md`, `05-search-and-similarity.md`, `06-rows-and-recommendations.md`, `07-client-api.md`, `08-operations.md`, `09-roadmap.md`, `10-telemetry-and-dashboards.md`, `decisions/README.md`, `decisions/0006-server-composed-home.md`, `decisions/0011-*.md`, `decisions/0014-absence-is-not-zero.md`, `decisions/0020-derived-state-carries-its-fingerprint.md`, `README.md` (repo root), `CLAUDE.md`
- Create: the ADRs Step 10 names, numbered from whatever `decisions/README.md` holds when this runs

- [ ] **Step 1: `06-rows-and-recommendations.md` — the document this milestone *is*, and it has no markers to retire**

Four corrections and one addition. Each states **what shipped and why**, in the PRD's own voice, with the reasoning behind a link. Never a deletion: a reader who remembers the old text needs to find out what happened to it.

**(a) The provider table is annotated nine-of-ten.** Ten rows ship as ten shipped providers today. `CuratedProvider` — *"Fires when: Fresh LLM rows exist"* — has no `curated_rows` table, no `LLMRow`, and no `LLMClient` implementation; PRD 02 already says M8 owns the family whole. Annotate the row rather than delete it, in the shape PRD 02 uses:

> `CuratedProvider` | ⏳ **M8.** `curated_rows`, `LLMRow` and the `LLMClient` implementation that fills them are M8's, together with `POST /admin/rows/regenerate`. Hydrating a table whose generator does not exist would fix that table's shape before anything had tried to fill it — the `search_queries` failure [10](10-telemetry-and-dashboards.md) argues at length, one milestone early. Boundary call 2.

And the sentence under the table — *"Adding a row type is a subclass and a registration. Nothing else changes."* — is now a **tested claim** rather than an aspiration, because Task 28's registry holds nine and the composition point is a registration. Say that it was checked, and by what.

**(b) The taste centroid's rating substitution, which is a new marker rather than a corrected one.** The Taste section reads:

> The **taste centroid** is the mean embedding of recently watched and highly rated titles, computed per user and cached.

**There is no rating anywhere in this system.** `WatchState` has no `rating` field and no `favorite`; `SourceWatchState` carries neither; Emby exposes both a user rating and `IsFavorite` and the adapter reads neither. `RediscoverProvider`'s own row in the table says *"Watched > 2 years ago, **rated highly**"* on the same evidence. **M7 does not invent a rating column** — it substitutes the engagement signal it actually has (`played`, `play_count`, completion) and says so here:

> 🔶 **"Highly rated" is substituted, not implemented.** There is no rating on `WatchState`, on `SourceWatchState` or on any port; M7's centroid and `RediscoverProvider` both use the engagement signal that exists — played, play count and completion — which is a *proxy for* rating and not the same thing: a film watched twice to completion and a film rated 2/10 and finished out of stubbornness are indistinguishable to it. Landing a real rating is a source-port change plus a contract case plus a live verification, against a field no client can set yet; it is **unassigned** and named here rather than left implied.

That marker is the important half. PRD 06 today asserts a taste model built on data the system has never held, and a reader has no way to know.

**(c) "Builds the top N concurrently" is corrected rather than implemented.** Boundary call 8, and it is a correctness statement rather than a performance preference:

> The home service collects all proposals, sorts by score, applies diversity constraints, **builds the top N sequentially**, drops any that build empty, and returns them. **Sequentially, not concurrently, and the reason is correctness.** `AsyncSession` is explicitly not safe for concurrent use — two coroutines awaiting on one session interleave on one connection — so `asyncio.gather` over providers sharing the request's session is not slower or faster, it is a corruption that *usually works*: two short reads frequently complete, and the failure is an intermittent `InvalidRequestError` or a result set attributed to the wrong query, under load. The two ways out are both worse at this scale — a session per row is nine connections for one home screen, i.e. pool exhaustion at one concurrent user against a default pool, and a semaphore has no lane to belong to ([01](01-architecture.md)'s concurrency table has none, and [08](08-operations.md) already retracted "concurrency per lane" as a setting because *"a setting cannot be added ahead of the mechanism it would bound"*). Every provider's query is a bounded local read, and `usher.home.compose.duration` with `usher.row.build.duration`'s per-provider breakdown is what makes revisiting this a number rather than an argument. Task 34 measured it; the figure is below.

**Carry Task 34's measured number in.** A boundary call with a number attached is a decision; the same call without one is a preference.

**(d) The caching table is reconciled with what Task 31 shipped**, row by row, and two of its five rows are false today:

| Row | What it says | What it must say |
|---|---|---|
| Built rows | "Per-row TTL, in-process" | whatever Task 31 shipped, named as shipped or marked ⏳ if it did not |
| Composed home screen | "~30 s per user" | same; and if there is no cache, say so — an un-cached screen that composes in single-digit milliseconds is a better answer than a documented cache nothing implements |
| **Neighbour tables** | **"Rebuilt on embedding change"** | **false, and it was false in M6 too.** Nothing rebuilds `title_neighbors` on any trigger; `usher similar --rebuild` is an operator's or a cron entry's job, and M6 recorded this as *"the milestone's one honest freshness gap"*. M7 narrows it: Task 35 adds `blend_fingerprint`, so "were these rows computed under the current blend?" is now a query and `usher.similarity.neighbors.stale` is a gauge — but the *other-title-was-embedded* half remains undecidable per row and stays an operator's job. State both halves |
| Curated rows | "Until regenerated" | ⏳ M8, with `CuratedProvider` |
| **Taste centroid** | **"Invalidated on watch-state change"** | **as written this is Trap 5.** The nightly walk merges up to 1,126,789 watch states; invalidating a centroid per merged row is a fan-out per row per night, which is exactly the reason [07](07-client-api.md) already says the walk deliberately publishes no `watchstate.updated`. Correct it to what Group G shipped — fingerprinted rather than TTL'd, driven by the push lane and by demand reads, never by the merge path |

And the sentence after the table — *"Rows are recomputed lazily and served stale while refreshing, so the home screen never blocks on a slow row"* — describes a background refresher. If Task 31 did not build one, it is corrected to what it did build, not left as a claim about behaviour under load that nothing produces.

**(e) `RowCard` carries no artwork field.** PRD 06 describes `RowCard` as carrying *"artwork refs, year, rating, progress"*. There is no `Image` table, no `images` column and no `poster_path` on `titles`. Boundary call 3, and it reuses M5's sentence from one route over verbatim because the question is identical: *"an empty list would be indistinguishable from a film with no cast."* A `RowCard` with `"artwork": null` on every card of every row is a client-side branch that never takes its other arm, and the day M9 fills it every client that shipped against the null already renders without it. (`rating` on the same line is the same problem from (b) and gets the same marker.)

Add the TOAST note, because someone will measure this again: 1,128 halfvec lanes is 2,256 bytes plus a header, past Postgres's ~2 kB inline threshold, so the heap holds 1,096 kB of pointers and TOAST holds 43 MB, and every genome read pays a TOAST fetch. **(a) The three corrected MovieLens numbers**, each with the measurement rather than a silent edit:

| PRD 04 says | Measured | Note |
|---|---|---|
