**(b) The licence row gets the right archive's clause**, and the archive choice is forced rather than preferred. `ml-32m` (05/2024, the newest full release) **dropped the genome entirely** — four members only. `ml-25m` has a genome and is the one archive whose licence says *"The user may not redistribute the data without separate permission."* `ml-latest` has a genome **and** the permissive clause — *"The user may redistribute the data set, including transformations, so long as it is distributed under these same license conditions."* Record all three, because the reason the licence row is right is only legible next to the two archives it is not.

Two more facts belong with it. `ml-latest`'s own README calls it *"a **development** dataset […] not an appropriate dataset for shared research results"*, which reads exactly like M6's `CachedDatasetFile` trap — an ETag-keyed cache in front of a moving file — and **measured, it has not moved in three years** (`Last-Modified: Thu, 20 Jul 2023 20:20:32 GMT`). IMDb regenerates daily and this does not, so the same cache behaves completely differently in front of it: same hazard shape, opposite conclusion, and that is worth a sentence rather than a shrug. And **range-fetching only the three members the importer reads (~96 MB of 335 MB) is possible and was deliberately declined** — `CachedDatasetFile` already handles resume, `If-Range` and the stale-snapshot interlock, and re-implementing that against per-member local headers to save 239 MB on a first bootstrap is new failure surface for a saving an operator pays once. Recorded as measured-and-declined rather than unconsidered.

**(c) Two physical properties of this snapshot that the importer must not silently depend on.** Both were measured for this plan and neither is documented by GroupLens anywhere:

> **`genome-scores.csv` is physically grouped and ordered.** 16,376 contiguous `movieId` runs, strictly increasing, every run exactly 1,128 rows with `tagId` 1…1128 in order. That is what makes a single-pass streaming importer that assembles one dense 1,128-lane vector per run possible without buffering the whole matrix. **It is a property of this snapshot, not a promise**, so the importer verifies it rather than assuming it — a run of the wrong length, an out-of-order `tagId`, or a `movieId` that reappears after its run closed is a hard failure with the offending row number, not a silently short vector. A vector assembled from a file that changed shape is a wrong answer that renders identically to a right one.

> **`links.csv`'s `tmdbId` is NOT unique — 162 duplicate rows over 38 ids — while `imdbId` is.** So the join to `titles` goes through `'tt' || lpad(imdbId, 7, '0')` and **never** through `tmdbId`: a `tmdbId` join fans a single TMDb id out across up to several MovieLens movies and would attach one film's genome vector to another's title. Measured over all 86,537 rows: `imdbId` is 7 characters wide on 79,978 and 8 on 6,559, never shorter, never empty. `'tt' || imdbId` happens to be correct today *and* `lpad` is the one to write, because the first silently depends on a padding convention the file documents nowhere and a single unpadded row would join to nothing rather than raise — the same family as M4's finding that 11 of 885 live Emby `Imdb` values were bare digits.

- [ ] **Step 10: The ADRs**

House style, in order, every one: **Context → Decision → Consequences → Evidence → Uncertainty**, with Consequences split into **Gained / Given up / Also / Rejected**. ADR-0018 is the model. `.claude/rules/prd-maintenance.md`: *"Write one only when the call was contested — where a reasonable person would choose differently, or where the reasoning would otherwise be lost."*

**Check `decisions/README.md` for the highest number when this task runs and number from there** — Task 3 wrote the row-ports ADR and may have taken more than one id. Two new ones qualify:

**The genome is one dense vector per title, not a tall relevance table.** Contested — PRD 02's own wording implied the tall form and a reasonable person reading "relevance scores" would build it. Decision: `halfvec(1128)`, one row per title. Evidence: 45 MB against **2,106 MB**, **47×**, measured on `pgvector/pgvector:pg17` (pgvector 0.8.6) at the real dimensions, against a database PRD 08 budgets at 8–12 GB total; `real[]` is 88 MB and worse than both because it has no operator class; a full pairwise cosine over all 16,376 vectors is **1.190 ms** on a `Seq Scan` with no index, because 16k rows never needs one. Gained: the similarity term is a single `<=>`, the operator `SimilarityService` already blends. Given up: the vector is TOASTed (2,256 bytes past the ~2 kB inline threshold), so every genome read pays a TOAST fetch — invisible at 16,376 rows, and one more reason the population is the genome's own and not the catalog's. Uncertainty: the archive is frozen and movies-only, so coverage decays with every release year, and the dense form assumes the matrix stays dense — which Step 4(c)'s verification is there to catch.

**Rows build sequentially, because `AsyncSession` is not concurrency-safe.** Contested — PRD 06 said *concurrently* in plain text and the correction is against a shipped document. Decision, consequences and rejected alternatives exactly as Step 1(c); Evidence is Task 34's measurement. **Uncertainty, stated rather than glossed:** this is right at nine bounded local reads and is *not* an argument that sequential is right at thirty providers or at a provider that calls out of process, and the thing that makes revisiting it a number rather than an argument is `usher.row.build.duration`'s per-provider breakdown. The way this ships wrong is that concurrent *usually works* — two short reads interleaved on one connection frequently complete, and the failure is an intermittent `InvalidRequestError` under load, in production — so the ADR is what stops a future contributor "optimising" it back.

**Three existing ADRs are amended rather than superseded**, per the rule that a resolved position is updated with its new evidence:

- **[ADR-0006](decisions/0006-server-composed-home.md)** — the ADR that governs this milestone, and its Consequences have never had a shipped system to describe. What got built: nine of ten providers, one response, no cursor, no envelope. Its central claim — *"One request paints a screen"* — gains Task 34's number.
- **[ADR-0020](decisions/0020-derived-state-carries-its-fingerprint.md)** — Task 35's amendment (`title_neighbors.blend_fingerprint`), plus the vindication of its own Uncertainty section: it said the fingerprint proves the *text* is current and not the *assembly rule*, and weight class B is exactly an assembly-rule change, handled by forcing a full column rewrite rather than by the predicate. Say that the concern was real and how it was met.
- **[ADR-0014](decisions/0014-absence-is-not-zero.md)** — two new sites: `GenomeRepository` returning `None` rather than a zero vector, and the blend scoring a half-covered pair `None` rather than `0.0`. The second is the first application where `0.0` is not merely uninformative but **unreachable by real data**, since every genome component is positive.

Add every new ADR to `decisions/README.md`.

```bash

import pathlib
import re

# `docs/prd/` plus the two documents at the repo root, and **not**
# `docs/plans/`. That exclusion is a correction rather than a convenience: a
# plan embeds PRD and ADR text whose links are relative to where the snippet
# will *live* (`docs/prd/`), not to where it is quoted. M5 was the first

roots = list(pathlib.Path("docs/prd").rglob("*.md"))

print("\n".join(bad) if bad else "OK")
EOF

```

The sweep is the only mechanism in this repository that can distinguish a provider whose ordering is correct from one whose test asserts membership.

- [ ] **Step 3: The migration chain, up and down — and two findings this step is required to record**

```bash
uv run alembic upgrade head
uv run alembic current
uv run alembic downgrade base

```

Empty → head → `downgrade base` → head, all clean. After `downgrade base`, **only `alembic_version` remains** and the extensions stay installed (M6 decided that: an extension is a database-level capability, not schema a migration owns). The second `upgrade head` from base must be clean and must produce the full table set.

**Finding 1 — the migration count.** The front matter says **four migrations, "and the plan says four so a fifth is a finding."** M6's plan said two and three shipped, and the extra one was legitimate and *unrecorded*, which is what made it worth flagging. M7 is already known to exceed four before this step runs:

- Task 35 ships a **fifth**, `title_neighbors.blend_fingerprint`, deliberately and with its reason — group F's genome migration lands earlier in the serial order, so amending it in place is not available.
- Task 36 may ship a **sixth** dropping `ix_titles_popularity`, conditional on its own measurement.

**Record the actual count, and for every migration past the fourth, record what it is, which task shipped it, and why it could not be folded into one of the four.** The rule is not that a fifth is forbidden; it is that a fifth arrives with an argument rather than by accretion.

**Finding 2 — the revision-id convention runs out inside this milestone.** The repository's ids spell `a…` → `f…` in chain order so that `ls` order matches migration order; M6 continued the scheme with `fa2b6c1e9d30`, `fb4e0a7d2c15`, `fc6d2b81a794`, and M6's own plan told M7 to *"confirm the first migration's docstring records that, so M7 does not re-derive it."*

**Three two-character prefixes remain — `fd`, `fe`, `ff` — and M7 plans four migrations.** The scheme is therefore exhausted at M7's *fourth* migration, before Task 35's fifth is even considered.

**Nothing breaks**, and saying so precisely is half the finding: alembic orders by `down_revision`, not lexically, so the chain is correct whatever the ids are. What is lost is the only thing the convention ever bought — that a directory listing reads in chain order. **The remedy is one sentence in a docstring:** when the two-character space is exhausted, extend by a character — `ff` → `ffa`, `ffb`, `ffc` — which still sorts after `fc` and after `ff`, is unbounded, and keeps `ls` order forever. Record the rule in the first M7 migration that needs it and in `CLAUDE.md`, so the next milestone does not re-derive it the way this one had to.

Weight class B changes `search_document`'s expression, which is precisely the category the diff will not see. **Read the migration; do not trust the diff.**

`cp .env.example .env`, one `USHER_SECRET_KEY`, **nothing else** — no exported variables, no hand-edits. That is the README's own first step and it is what produced 461 errors at M5. The mechanism, restated because M7 adds settings and therefore reintroduces the hazard: `.env` has two readers with different vocabularies. Docker Compose reads it to substitute `${…}` into `compose.yml`; pydantic-settings reads the same file as a settings source with `extra="forbid"`. A compose-only variable is therefore an *extra* input to `Settings`. **The suite cannot see this** — `tests/conftest.py::clean_environment` neutralises the `env_file` source deliberately, and the M5 errors came from the one path that fixture cannot reach (`tests/integration/conftest.py::_upgrade_head`, session-scoped, which saves and restores `os.environ` but has no way to hide a *file*). A clean-checkout run is not redundant with `uv run pytest`; it is the only thing that exercises the file source at all.

M6's clean checkout ran **2,433 passed, 5 skipped — identical to the working tree.** M7's must match its own working-tree number the same way.

**And the embedding extra must be ABSENT**, because a bare `uv sync` is the shipped default and **every M7 provider must degrade rather than fail without it**. This is the claim with the most surface in M7 and the least coverage anywhere else:

- `BecauseYouWatchedProvider` reads `title_neighbors`, which is built from embeddings — with none, the table is empty and the provider must **return nothing**, not fall back to popular titles.
- `GenreAffinityProvider` reads the taste centroid, which is a mean of embeddings — with none, there is no centroid, and `HomeService` must **compose without one**.
- The genome term needs no embedder at all, but its *candidate pool* comes from `title_embeddings`, so with no embedder there are no seeds and `usher similar --rebuild` writes nothing — and should say so rather than report success over an empty population.
- `GET /home` and `usher home` must both answer, with whichever rows have data.

The expected outcome is **a shorter home screen, not a crash, not an empty 500, and not a generic one.** Run `usher home` against a seeded catalog with no embedder and record what came back — which providers fired, which returned nothing, and whether anything returned a *generic* row, which is the failure this milestone's front matter names as the one that survives review.

Three settings checks, all of which must pass and two of which have teeth: `test_every_setting_is_read_by_something` (every new field is *read* in `src/` in the same commit — this one is also the collateral kill that ruled out M5's naive fix), the two scanners `test_every_usher_variable_in_env_example_is_a_setting_or_compose_reserved` and `test_every_variable_compose_substitutes_is_a_setting_or_compose_reserved` (both needed — the compose-side one regex-scans the *whole* of `compose.yml`, because a variable added to a `volumes:` line is the same hazard), and `test_env_example_ships_the_defaults`. **Any case written for these must pass `_env_file=` explicitly**, since the autouse fixture neutralises the class-level `env_file` and a case relying on it proves nothing.

- [ ] **Step 6: The whole-suite mutation sweep**

Every mutation named in Tasks 1–36, run in sequence against the **full** suite rather than its own task's selection. A per-task sweep cannot see collateral in another file, which is the entire point — M4's found `usable-ids-filters-nothing` caught by a case in a different file's *second* item, and M6's found the milestone's headline refusal property guarded by exactly one case in 2,433, and not the one the plan named.

```bash
cd /home/anirudhlath/code/usher
find src tests -name __pycache__ -type d -exec rm -rf {} +
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
git status --porcelain          # must be empty before starting
uv run pytest 2>&1 | tail -1    # baseline green, and record the wall clock
```

**M6's harness rules, enforced by the harness rather than by the operator's attention.** Each is here because it produced a wrong result once:

1. **Validate every mutation with `compile(source, path, "exec")` — `ast.parse` is not sufficient and M6 proved it.** `'continue' not properly in loop` is raised at the *compile* stage, not the parse stage, so a broken mutation dry-ran clean, the suite died at collection in 1 s, and the harness scored `KILLED`. This is trap rule 3 failing in a way the rule as originally written did not cover.
2. **`ERROR collecting` plus `SyntaxError` in a run is `BROKEN-MUTATION`.** Not `KILLED`.
3. **A run that collected zero tests is `DID-NOT-RUN`.** Never `KILLED`. M4 scored three mutations as caught having measured nothing.
4. **Mutate in place, never in a `/tmp` copy** — `cp -r` copies `.venv/bin/*`, whose shebangs point back into the *original* venv, so a mutation in the copy is never imported and the suite runs green proving nothing. If a copy is unavoidable, **rewrite the shebangs**. If every mutation in a sweep survives, that is this trap and not a finding.
5. **`cp` backups, never `git checkout --`**, which clobbers uncommitted work in the same file.
6. **A signal handler, or a `git status` check after any interruption.** M6 learned this the hard way: **SIGTERM skips the `finally`** and leaves the tree mutated; the `cp` backup is what recovered it.
7. **The target string must appear exactly once** in the file before substitution.
8. **A wall-clock bound**, so a non-converging change is `HUNG` rather than read as a mutation nothing observed. M6 used 420 s against a 69.6 s baseline; scale it to M7's measured baseline.
9. **A mutation must be the change the plan names, not a change that happens to break the statement.** M6's clearest example: `updated_at = now()` "dropped" spelled as a *replacement* produced a duplicate `SET`, i.e. a SQL error and a false `KILLED`; re-run as an actual deletion it survived, as predicted. **A mutation that breaks the statement rather than changing the behaviour measures the parser, not the suite.**

**The headline mutations this milestone's cases must kill.** A sweep that does not kill these has found something, and each is named with the property it attacks:

| Mutation | Must fail, and by position |
|---|---|
| **a provider's `ORDER BY` key removed** | the milestone's headline failure. It must fail **by position**, on a case that seeded a distractor a broken build ranks first — a membership assertion is satisfied by returning the whole library in physical order. Run it against **every one of the nine**, not one representative |
| **the popular-titles fallback introduced** into a provider that should return nothing | the row that "looks personalised and is not, on a household that has watched nothing". Assert the *absent* row, not an empty one — an empty row and an absent row are different states and a generic row is neither |
| **`next_up` returns the first unplayed episode** | valid, populated, correctly shaped, and wrong forever for every series in the library. Also the sibling: an episode from a season the user has not started |
| **the taste centroid's sign flipped** | returns the user's *least* favourite genre with total confidence, and nothing raises |
| **the composed screen's diversity constraint deleted** | three consecutive similarity rows, or one family filling the screen |
| **weight class B's fingerprint moved on one side only** | Trap 2 — the Python composer and `_FINGERPRINT_SQL` are two spellings of one function. Move one and every credited title matches the stale predicate **forever**: re-embed, write a fingerprint the SQL cannot reproduce, re-claim next pass. **An infinite backfill that never errors — so bound this one or the sweep hangs**, and score it `HUNG` rather than either outcome if it exceeds the bound. `services/search.py:154-158` already says the two must move together; this mutation is what proves the suite agrees |
| **`_WEIGHTS["tags"]` deleted** (Task 35) | must fail on a genome-bearing pair's *position*, not on a weights-dict equality assertion |
| **the genome cosine scored `0.0` instead of `None`** on a half-covered pair (Task 35) | ADR-0014's newest site, and the one where the wrong value is unreachable by real data |
| **`blend_fingerprint`'s comparison inverted or its predicate emptied** (Task 35) | a gauge that always reads zero is indistinguishable from a fresh table, which is the whole reason the column exists |

**Named survivors are recorded as equivalent, with the argument, and never quietly dropped.** Each must survive **for the stated reason** rather than for a different one, and **a survivor this plan did not name is a missing test, and writing it is part of this step.** The precedent is exact: M5 named six expected survivors, five survived for the stated reason, and the sixth was *killed* by a case that pins the field directly rather than by the security property the plan reasoned about — recorded so nobody read that kill as evidence the flag was load-bearing. M6 recorded eleven survivors the same way and found one real coverage gap in the process.

For each survivor write: **what it is, why it cannot be observed today, what would make it observable, and what change in the repository would turn it into a real bug.** "Equivalent mutant" with no argument attached is indistinguishable from "we did not write that test."

```bash
git status --porcelain          # empty again
uv run pytest 2>&1 | tail -1    # green again
```

```bash

uv run pytest tests/unit/test_no_third_party_data.py
python3 - <<'EOF'
import pathlib
import re

roots = list(pathlib.Path("docs/prd").rglob("*.md"))
roots += [pathlib.Path("CLAUDE.md"), pathlib.Path("README.md")]
bad = []
for md in roots:
    for link in re.findall(r'\]\(([^)#][^)]*\.md)\)', md.read_text()):
        if not (md.parent / link).resolve().exists():
            bad.append(f"{md}: {link}")
print("\n".join(bad) if bad else "OK")
EOF
```

Expected: `OK`, and every check green. **Scoped to `docs/prd/` plus the two root documents and deliberately not `docs/plans/`** — a plan embeds PRD and ADR text whose links are relative to where the snippet will *live*, not to where it is quoted, and that scoping is exactly what makes a green result mean something rather than being a formality that passes for the wrong reason.

`test_no_third_party_data.py` scans four ways and **M7 adds fixtures to three of the shapes it checks**, so this is a live check: IMDb ids must be in the `tt99`/`nm99` band, every id in a fixture must be ≥ 90,000,000, and **a credits entry is a flat JSON object carrying `original_name`, which is exactly the shape `_TMDB_EXPORT_RECORD` matches** — so a cast fixture with a small `id` fails that guard. M7's new fixture families are the ones to check by name: cast/crew payloads, `belongs_to_collection`, and any MovieLens row shape. **Every genome `movieId` and every `links.csv` row in a fixture is synthetic**, and Task 36's measurement in `docs/` is the other thing this scan now reads.

- [ ] **Step 8: A live end-to-end run, bounded and stated**

In the format M3/M4/M5/M6's live sections use, driven from a throwaway script outside the working tree, writing **no credential, token, user id or host into the repo**.

**In scope:**

- a real catalog — `bootstrap --phase all` (~3 min, no API key) plus `--phase movielens`, with the archive's wall clock, the rows imported, and the NIC delta recorded;
- `usher derive` bounded over a slice of `raw_payloads`, with the people/credits/collections counts it produced and the wall clock;
- a real household's watch state **if one is reachable** — `usher sync` against the configured Emby source, **bounded in the iterator, never with `max_pages`** (exhausting `max_pages` raises `PortDataMalformed` and records `FAILED`; it is the walk's dead-man's switch, not a bound, and a probe that ignored this once issued several hundred requests against a shared server before it was killed);
- **a composed screen printed** — `usher home` and `GET /home` for that household, with every row's kind, its card count, its reason string, and the order they came back in. **Print the actual screen**, because the whole premise of this milestone is that a wrong one is indistinguishable from a right one to a test, and a human reading ten real rows is the only oracle that exists;
- `usher.home.compose.duration` and the per-provider `usher.row.build.duration` breakdown, which is boundary call 8's number and the thing that makes revisiting sequential composition an argument with evidence.

**Deliberately not in scope, named rather than implied:** curated/LLM rows (M8); artwork (M9); `GET /home` under any concurrency (the sequential build's behaviour under load is exactly what `usher.row.build.duration` exists to inform later, and one run does not measure it); full TMDb enrichment of the owned library (hours of API calls for a screen that composes from what is already there); more than one household; more than one source; and GPU embedding throughput, still unmeasured for the same reason M6 declined it.

**Report guess by guess, refutations first, with a confirmed / refuted / still unverified column.** M3's live run found the write-back route was simply wrong; M4's found the exact-name tier matches ~74% where the plan expected "almost nothing"; M5's found four of thirteen guesses wrong; **M6's found five of seven.** **A live run that confirms everything it expected is a run that did not look hard enough.** Candidates this run can settle: that nine providers all fire on a real household (they will not — say which returned nothing and whether that was correct); that `usher derive` finds credits in every payload; that the sequential build is fast enough that nobody wants it concurrent; that `next_up` is right on a real, messy watch history with partially-watched seasons and out-of-order plays, which is the single hardest thing in this milestone to get right and the easiest to get plausibly wrong.
